about: Radio and intercom for chapter 4: into the LM. The crawl through the tunnel, the LM cabin, undocking (GET 107:47:56), the Command Module coming round to look at the legs, separation, and go for powered descent. t = GET (seconds from liftoff); cue lines play on events. America is the Command and Service Module, Challenger the Lunar Module. Original lines in the style of Apollo procedure; not quotes.

lines.text: Your turn. Probe and drogue are stowed, and the tunnel is clear.
Come on through. Head first, hand over hand. Mind the hatch rim at the bottom.
Take your time. Grab the tunnel wall and pull yourself along, nice and easy.
Welcome aboard Challenger. Your restraints are by your feet.
America here. I'm putting the drogue and the hatch back in. Close yours on your side.
Challenger, Houston. You are go for undocking.
Roger, go for undocking. Thank you, Houston.
Two minutes. Are you ready, Challenger?
Ready when you are, America.
Undocking in ten seconds.
Undock. We are apart. Backing away now.
Look up through the docking window. There she goes.
I'm coming round in front of you, so I can see your legs.
All four legs are down and locked, and the probes look good. You are a beautiful sight, Challenger.
Thank you, America. See you in three days.
Separation burn in one minute. Stand by.
Burn complete. Opening it up. Good luck, Challenger.
America, Houston. We see a good circularization burn.
Challenger, Houston. All your systems look good going round.
Challenger, Houston. If you read, you are go for powered descent.
Roger, go for PDI. Here we go.
